title: Tapping a router tray chip places a stray router at the chip's map tile, consuming inventory
detail: The arming press sets app.placing then returns; that same tap's release (moved=false) submits Cmd_Place_Router at the chip's world tile — row ~28, in-bounds on the 40x30 map — consuming a router. No guard that the press began on the tray.
recommended_fix: Track press origin: when a tray chip is hit, mark it (app.press_on_tray=true). Gate the release placement on that flag being false — only submit Cmd_Place_Router when the press began on the map, not on a tray chip.

title: synth_sting's descending_alarm parameter is declared but never used
evidence:
synth_sting :: proc(freqs: []f32, note_seconds: f32, descending_alarm: bool) -> rl.Sound {
(The body — the sample loop, the WAV builder — never references descending_alarm; grep finds the identifier only on this signature line.)
detail: descending_alarm is declared but never read in the body; init_audio passes true (crisis) vs false (win) expecting a different waveform that never happens.
recommended_fix: Either implement the descending-alarm behavior (reverse freq order when true) or drop the parameter and the two boolean arguments at the call sites.
